haiku-low.q1: A domain-events topic message, produced by the existing outbox relay, which the DSP consumer reads.
haiku-low.q2: DSP matches active subscriptions by account_id and event_type, inserting one row per match. A unique event_id plus subscription_id with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING blocks duplicates.
haiku-low.q3: HMAC-SHA256 over t + '.' + stored body bytes, keyed by the subscription secret. It is recomputed with a fresh t on every attempt, including replays.
haiku-low.q4: 2xx marks done. 410 marks dead and disables the subscription. Other 4xx marks dead. Retryable failures wait for retry until the 8th failure, then dead.
haiku-low.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails.
haiku-low.q6: In the deliveries table in the webhook service's own Postgres, with status, attempt_count, next_attempt_at, last_status_code and last_error columns.
haiku-low.q7: It waits as a pending row with next_attempt_at set to now plus the gap. A sender poll claims it once due, so no queue delay is used.
haiku-low.q8: The row stays in sending until lease_until (claim time plus 60 s) expires. The next polling worker re-claims it, and the receiver may see it twice.
haiku-low.q9: In the deliveries table as status=dead rows, not a separate queue. Replay resets it to pending, attempt_count 0, next_attempt_at now, same id. Disabled subscription replay returns 409.
haiku-low.q10: The X-Webhook-Id header, which is the delivery id. It never changes across attempts or replays.
haiku-low.q11: When a claimed pending delivery's subscription is disabled, it is marked dead with reason subscription_disabled and no HTTP request is sent.
haiku-low.q12: Yes. There is no ordering between events, and retries can reorder deliveries.

sonnet.q1: Events on the domain-events topic/queue, consumed by the DSP consumer; the trigger is produced by the existing outbox relay.
sonnet.q2: DSP matches active subscriptions (same account_id, event_type in list or '*') and inserts one DLV row per match in one transaction, committed before ack. A unique key on event_id + subscription_id with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes redelivered/duplicate inserts no-ops.
sonnet.q3: HMAC-SHA256 with the subscription's decrypted secret over t + '.' + the stored body bytes (header X-Webhook-Signature t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>). It is redone with a fresh t on every attempt, including replays.
sonnet.q4: 2xx: done (delivered). 410: dead (reason gone) and the subscription is disabled (disabled_reason gone). Other 4xx: dead (client_error). Retryable (408, 429, 5xx, timeout, connection error): back to pending with a delay, or dead (retries_exhausted) if the 8th attempt fails.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails (next_attempt_at = now + 2m).
sonnet.q6: In the DLV store, the `deliveries` table in the webhook service's own Postgres: status, attempt_count, next_attempt_at, last_status_code, last_error (plus lease_until, dead_reason, dead_at, body bytes).
sonnet.q7: It waits as a pending row in the deliveries table with next_attempt_at set (now + gap). A sender's 1s poll claims it once it is due; queue delays are not used.
sonnet.q8: The job row stays in `sending` until lease_until (claim time + 60 s) expires, then the next polling worker re-claims it. The lost try still counts toward the 8 because attempt_count was bumped at claim, and the receiver may see the request twice.
sonnet.q9: There is no separate queue: the DLQ is the deliveries rows with status=dead. Replay (via admin API) flips the record back to pending with attempt_count reset to 0 and next_attempt_at = now, keeping the same id.
sonnet.q10: The delivery id sent as the X-Webhook-Id header. It never changes across attempts or replays.
sonnet.q11: When a sender claims such a delivery and finds the subscription disabled, it is marked dead with reason subscription_disabled, with no HTTP request sent.
sonnet.q12: Yes. There is no ordering between events, and retries reorder things.
